images.prompt: Create a single photorealistic, landscape-format historical reenactment still. Natural color as if professionally photographed on location; human, restrained, materially credible, candid composition. No captions, letters, maps, labels, watermark, collage or painted surface. Meuse-Argonne near Châtel-Chéhéry France, October 8 1918. From behind a small U.S. infantry patrol slipping single file along a wooded ravine, early autumn foliage mottled green, ochre, slopes concealing the opposing guns, damp ground, subdued morning daylight. 1918 American olive-drab wool service coats, puttees, shallow round M1917 steel helmets, cartridge belts, long bolt-action service rifles. No 1940s helmets, modern packs, or trench skyline.

images.title: Collecting the surrendered weapons
images.caption: The patrol has taken prisoners. Collecting arms and moving captives now occupy men who were sent to silence the guns.

Natural color as if professionally photographed on location; human, restrained, materially credible, candid composition. No captions, letters, maps, labels, watermark, collage or painted surface. WWI Meuse-Argonne Forest France in October 1918. Close foreground study of DISCARDED German long bolt-action rifles resting horizontally against each other on the leaf-littered earth, stocks and barrels clearly visible beside a shallow earth bank. Mid-distance: unarmed, barehanded German POWs in wool field-grey caps sitting in a small group against the bank, empty hands visible, with no rifles slung on them. One standing American guard at the edge facing away wears a broad flat shallow brimmed 1917 Brodie helmet and carries the only raised rifle. No modern gear, no heroic protagonist. Somber, calm, autumn morning.
